Second Verified -1 on 1731 (run 31734135055) triaged and NOT attributed to this change.

macos-latest/py3.13 only: 1 failed, 12849 passed. Failure is 'worker gw1 crashed while running tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_hardening.py::test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer' — a worker kill with no traceback and no assertion.

The discriminating evidence is change 1734: it contains this exact commit plus one more, and it passed macos-latest/py3.13 with identical renderer code. Combined with this diff touching no runtime file (portability rubric, docs/plan-review-gate.md, AGENTS.md, two portability test modules) and the full unit suite passing locally at 12853/0, the failure cannot be attributed here.

Rather than retry silently, the nondeterminism is filed as bug 0078-fa3e-05d1-4e12 (linked discovered_from) with the run as evidence — the existing xdist-crash tickets c89f and fade cover the opcert test, not this one. Leading hypothesis, explicitly unconfirmed: the pandoc-driven corpus comparison exceeds the 300s per-test timeout on the contended macOS lane, which story 271c recorded for a sibling wiki-render test.

Rechecked 1731 with that reasoning stated in the Gerrit comment, which is the narrow carve-out the rule in 9b79-56ba-0d16-4c49 allows: a resource-contention worker kill on an untouched subsystem, not a nondeterministic assertion in this diff.
